Other Ways to Pledge

There are several ways to support the VMI Foundation or the VMI Keydet Club through an estate plan or other planned gift.

Bequests in a Will or TrustLeave a specific dollar amount, personal property, real estate, or a percentage of your estate to VMI.
Beneficiary DesignationsName VMI as a primary or contingent beneficiary on an IRA, 401(k), 403(b), bank account, investment account, or life insurance policy.
Charitable Remainder Trusts or “Give It Twice” TrustsEstablish a trust that provides income to a spouse or children for life or for a set period, with the remaining balance later transferred to VMI.
Charitable Gift AnnuitiesMake a gift in exchange for fixed lifetime payments for one or two people, with the remaining funds later supporting VMI.
Donor Advised FundsContribute to a donor advised fund, receive an immediate tax deduction, and recommend future gifts to VMI.
Charitable EndowmentsCreate an endowed fund through a will or trust. The principal is invested, and annual income supports a chosen area of VMI.

Planned gifts may qualify donors for membership in the Legacy Society, which includes invitations to special events, recognition in publications, and a Legacy Pin.

Featured Brother Rats

Meet members of the VMI Class of 2001 and learn where life has taken them since graduation.

Carl Haas

Assistant Men's Lacrosse Coach, Frostburg State University

What are you doing now? I am an Assistant Men's Lacrosse Coach at Frostburg State in Maryland. I have been a college coach for 23 years and have been all over on this journey. I met my wife, Judy, while coaching at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. We married in 2015 and have three kids. I have always been into video games, but with three kids and my work schedule, I get one hobby, and it is still playing video games.

Most memorable moment or biggest takeaway from VMI VMI taught me how to grow, adapt, overcome obstacles, and find a way to get something done. It was the right place for me, and I loved my time at VMI.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion? I think it is that feeling of slipping right back into conversations and friendships that pick up as if no time had gone by. We will rehash some of the same stories, but it is about feeling connected to people I depended on, looked up to, and who helped me grow.

The Institute did a lot of molding, but the people to my left and right did more. I cannot wait to see you all again.

Brandon Bowman

Commander, Jacksonville District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers

I am in my final year as Commander of the Jacksonville District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The district is currently in its 26th year of restoring the Everglades, the largest ecosystem restoration project in the known galaxy. Beyond the Everglades, we oversee 28 coastal storm risk management projects, manage water levels in Lake Okeechobee, and maintain Florida's deep-water harbors.

Next summer, I will most likely retire from the Army and move back to Pennsylvania. My wife and I recently purchased an old mill house built in 1750 that was once owned by my great-great-grandparents. It is only about a mile and a half from where I grew up and where my parents still live.

Since we are close to Orlando, we have been spending long weekends at Disney World and Universal Studios. In my free time, I work on a 1962 TVR Grantura and a 1967 Land Rover Series IIA. I also recently bought a pinball machine, which has turned out to be one of the best dumb purchases I have ever made.

VMI reflection One of my favorite memories is hearing the Christmas carols played after Taps during the holiday season. The image that stays with me is walking through the stoops after dark, seeing the lights glowing in barracks, and watching cadets move through Jackson Arch.

What are you most excited about for the 25th Reunion? Despite multiple deployments and a busy Army career, I have never missed a class reunion, and I hope to keep that streak alive. It is always great to see everyone again, catch up on where life has taken us, and discover just how much older, and in many cases wider, we have all become.
